facts.text: Lolo sits at the confluence of Lolo Creek and the Bitterroot River, serving as a gateway to the Bitterroot Mountains and the expansive Lolo National Forest.
Lewis and Clark camped at Travelers' Rest near Lolo from September 9–11, 1805, planning their westward route after a harsh winter.
The Lolo Trail, a rugged path over the Bitterroot Mountains, was a vital hunting and trade corridor for the Salish, Kootenai, and Nez Perce long before settlers.
Lolo’s name may stem from French fur trapper Lawrence Rence, or from “Le Louis,” the French name for Meriwether Lewis, reflecting early trade ties.
The 2017 Lolo Peak Fire burned thousands of acres southwest of town, forcing evacuations and closing U.S. Highway 12 for weeks.
